Verified by the two new tests in internal/cli/domain_lens_test.go (spec test 1): TestReview_DeactivatedRoleNamedDisabledBySpec and TestAudit_DeactivatedRoleNamedDisabledBySpec each deactivate one role of a two/three-role user corpus, assert the survivor still emits, the deactivated role emits no prompt, and its skipped_roles reason is disabled-by-spec; the review half also asserts regression is still reported with no-baseline, pinning that the new reason is added to the existing ones rather than substituting for them.

tasks.title: Refuse a phase with no roles
tasks.acceptance: Emitting prompts for a phase whose active roles are all dropped exits 2. The message renders as every <phase> role is deactivated by this spec followed by the ids, with the phase word taken from PhaseReviewers or PhaseAuditors. The hint reads re-enable at least one role, or remove the enabled: false entries.
tasks.closed_reason:
- The empty-phase refusal now renders the full §2.5 message: refuseEmptyPhase(phase string, disabled []string) in internal/cli/review.go emits "every <phase> role is deactivated by this spec: <ids>" with the phase word taken from the engine.PhaseReviewers/engine.PhaseAuditors value passed by each caller and the ids sorted (on a defensive copy) and comma-separated, plus the hint "re-enable at least one role, or remove the enabled: false entries" passed to output.Error. It still exits 2.
- Both phases refuse: internal/cli/review.go passes engine.PhaseReviewers with disabledRoles and internal/cli/audit.go passes engine.PhaseAuditors with its own disabledRoles (audit already had the call site from drop-outside-corpus; only the id argument was added).
- Verified by the two new tests in internal/cli/domain_lens_test.go (spec test 7): TestReview_EmptyPhaseMessageRendersSortedIDs and TestAudit_EmptyPhaseMessageRendersSortedIDs each deactivate two corpus roles, require exit 2 and an empty stdout, and decode tp's JSON error object off stderr to assert the message and hint verbatim — "every reviewers role is deactivated by this spec: architect, tester" and "every auditors role is deactivated by this spec: alpha, zeta". The role files are written in reverse alphabetical order, so a rendering echoing corpus order rather than sorting would fail.
- Dogfooded with a freshly built /tmp/tp-dev/tp: a two-reviewer spec deactivating both prints {"error":"every reviewers role is deactivated by this spec: architect, tester","code":2,"hint":"re-enable at least one role, or remove the enabled: false entries"} and exits 2; tp lint spec/0.32.0.md exit 0.
- Gate run with separate exit codes: go test ./... exit 0, golangci-lint run exit 0 (0 issues).
Out of scope: the sibling tasks own the filtering of the id list to spec-deactivated ids only (empty-phase-id-list), excluding the built-in regression role (regression-not-counted), proving the refusal precedes EnsureReviewState and the audit snapshot (refusal-before-writes), and the spec-coverage refusal / skipped_roles / emission-only scoping.

tasks.title: List only spec-deactivated ids
tasks.acceptance: The empty-phase id list carries only the ids this spec deactivated, sorted comma-separated. Ids already absent through domains or a missing role file are excluded. A phase emptied partly by domains names only the deactivated ones.
tasks.closed_reason:
- The empty-phase id list carries only the ids this spec deactivated with enabled: false, sorted and comma-separated: the drop set is computed in engine.ResolveOverrideFocus over the ACTIVE role set, which is post-domain-filter (ResolveActiveCorpus filters by domains before the resolver sees the panel) and contains only roles with a corpus file, so an id absent for either reason takes the existing 'matches no active role' path and contributes no drop.
- Verified by the new mixed-case fixture TestReview_EmptyPhaseNamesOnlySpecDeactivatedIDs (internal/cli/domain_lens_test.go): a reviewer corpus of aardvark (domains: [prose], filtered out on a software spec), beta and delta (active), with tp.review_roles deactivating all three plus a ghost id that has no role file; the phase empties and the refusal reads exactly 'every reviewers role is deactivated by this spec: beta, delta'. 'aardvark' sorts first, so an implementation keyed on the frontmatter entries rather than the drop set would lead the list with it and fail.
- TestAudit_EmptyPhaseNamesOnlySpecDeactivatedIDs pins the same rule on the auditor phase ('every auditors role is deactivated by this spec: beta, delta'), since both callers share the resolver.
- The rule is now stated where it is decided: comments on ResolveOverrideFocus's drop-set block (internal/engine/overrides.go) and on refuseEmptyPhase (internal/cli/review.go). No behavior change was required; the placement chosen by drop-outside-corpus already satisfied it, and the fixture locks it against a future implementation keyed on the frontmatter entries.
- Gate green before close: go test ./... exit 0, golangci-lint run exit 0 (checked as separate exit codes).

tasks.title: Exclude regression from the emptiness check
tasks.acceptance: The built-in regression role does not count as an active reviewer for the emptiness check. A review spec deactivating every corpus reviewer still exits 2. Test 9 passes.

tasks.title: Resolve roles ahead of every write
tasks.acceptance: Corpus resolution alongside override resolution run ahead of EnsureReviewState in tp review. They run ahead of the snapshot write in tp audit. Test 7 asserts a refused run writes no state directory, no state file, no round snapshot.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Corpus resolution and override layering now run ahead of every write tp review's emission path performs: the new resolveRolePanel (internal/cli/review.go) does ResolveActiveCorpus + ResolveOverrideFocus + the §2.3 drop + both §2.5 refusals in §2.6's order, and runReview calls it BEFORE loadReviewRoundState, which is where EnsureReviewState creates .tp-review/<spec>/ and state.json and WriteSnapshotAtomic writes snapshot-round-1.md; buildReviewPrompts now receives the resolved panel instead of resolving it itself.
- The same helper runs ahead of the snapshot write in tp audit: runAudit (internal/cli/audit.go) calls resolveRolePanel(specPath, engine.PhaseAuditors) before loadAuditSpec, which is the function that writes snapshot-audit-round-1.md; the 29-line inline corpus/override/refusal block was deleted and fmAudit replaced by panel.fm.
- Test 7 is asserted per command over that command's OWN artifacts by TestRefusals_WriteNothingBeforeRefusing (internal/cli/domain_lens_test.go): the review half (run WITHOUT --no-state, the only mode that arms the state lifecycle) asserts exit 2 plus NoDirExists on .tp-review/spec, NoFileExists on state.json and on snapshot-round-1.md; the audit half asserts exit 2 plus NoFileExists on snapshot-audit-round-1.md. The test was written first and verified failing against the unfixed tree with all four assertions red, so it discriminates.
- Review was ALSO broken, not just audit: pre-fix the review half left the state directory, state.json AND the round snapshot behind. Every pre-existing empty-phase review test passes --no-state, which skips the state lifecycle entirely and hid the bug.
- Gate green before closing: go test ./... exit 0, golangci-lint run exit 0 (checked as separate exit codes, not a && chain).

tasks.title: Refuse deactivating the spec-coverage auditor
tasks.acceptance: An auditor drop set containing spec-coverage exits 2 with the message spec-coverage cannot be deactivated: it carries the entire spec-derived checklist. The hint reads remove the enabled: false entry for spec-coverage. It fires even when other auditors remain active.
tasks.closed_reason:
- An auditor drop set containing spec-coverage exits 2 with the message "spec-coverage cannot be deactivated: it carries the entire spec-derived checklist": refuseSpecCoverageDeactivated(disabled []string) in internal/cli/audit.go scans the drop set returned by engine.ResolveOverrideFocus and calls output.Error(ExitUsage, ...) + os.Exit(ExitUsage) on a spec-coverage entry; verified by TestAudit_SpecCoverageCannotBeDeactivated asserting exit 2 and the message verbatim off the JSON error object on stderr.
- The hint reads "remove the enabled: false entry for spec-coverage": passed as output.Error's hint argument, both strings built from the existing roleSpecCoverage constant; verified by the same test's assert.Equal on the decoded hint field.
- It fires even when other auditors remain active: the check is a drop-set membership test, not an emptiness test, and runs before DropDisabledRoles/the empty-phase check (§2.6 precedence); verified by the test's corpus of two auditor role files (spec-coverage + keeper) where only spec-coverage is deactivated and keeper would still have emitted, plus an empty-stdout assertion that no prompt precedes the refusal.
- Dogfooded with the freshly built /tmp/tp-dev/tp against a copy of tp's own .tp/auditors corpus: the refusal returned the exact message, hint and exit 2. Gate green: go test ./... exit 0, golangci-lint run exit 0 (0 issues).

tasks.title: Key the refusal on the drop set
tasks.acceptance: The refusal keys on the drop set rather than on the frontmatter entry. Identical frontmatter exits 2 against an auditor corpus holding the spec-coverage role file but warns matches no active role against a populated corpus lacking it. A review_roles entry naming spec-coverage always takes the warning path.
tasks.closed_reason:
- The spec-coverage refusal is proven to key on the drop set rather than on the frontmatter entry: TestAudit_SpecCoverageRefusalKeysOnDropSet (internal/cli/domain_lens_test.go) runs both halves over the ONE shared const specCoverageDeactivatedSpec (tp.audit_roles naming spec-coverage with enabled: false) and varies only the .tp/auditors corpus via the new writeAuditorCorpusProject helper.
- Against an auditor corpus holding spec-coverage.json (plus keeper) the half asserts exit 2 with the verbatim refusal message and hint off the JSON error object, and an empty stdout; against a POPULATED corpus of keeper+second lacking that file the identical frontmatter asserts exit 0 with both corpus roles emitted and no spec-coverage prompt. The second half deliberately uses a populated rather than empty directory, since an empty .tp/auditors falls back to the embedded default corpus (which holds spec-coverage) and would re-arm the drop.
- The test was verified to discriminate the correct implementation from the plausible wrong one: with refuseSpecCoverageDeactivated temporarily fed a drop list built from fm.AuditRoles entries instead of the resolved drop set, the pre-existing TestAudit_SpecCoverageCannotBeDeactivated still PASSED while the new second half FAILED with exit 2 where 0 was required; the mutation was then reverted.
- A tp.review_roles entry naming spec-coverage always takes the warning path: TestReview_SpecCoverageEntryTakesWarningPath lays down .tp/auditors/spec-coverage.json (the exact disk state that makes tp audit refuse) plus a reviewers corpus without it, and asserts tp review exits 0 and emits the reviewer panel, so the review caller cannot trip the auditor refusal.
- The 'matches no active role' warning text itself is asserted at the engine layer by TestResolveOverrideFocus_SpecCoverageDropDependsOnCorpus (internal/engine/overrides_test.go), because output.Info is suppressed in the JSON mode every runTP call uses; it pins the drop set to [spec-coverage] against a panel holding the role, empty plus the verbatim audit_roles warning against a populated panel lacking it, and empty plus the review_roles warning for the review phase.
- Gate green, exit codes checked separately: go test ./... exit 0, golangci-lint run exit 0 (0 issues).

tasks.title: Report spec-coverage before empty phase
tasks.acceptance: The checks are decided in the order given by the precedence section. A spec tripping both refusals reports the spec-coverage one. Test 10 passes.
tasks.closed_reason:
- The §2.6 order is locked by TestAudit_SpecCoverageRefusalPrecedesEmptyPhase (internal/cli/domain_lens_test.go): a spec deactivating spec-coverage AND every other active auditor (corpus {spec-coverage, keeper}) trips both §2.5 refusals at once and reports the spec-coverage message and hint verbatim, with an assert.NotContains proving the empty-phase message never reaches the agent.
- No production change was needed: internal/cli/audit.go already decides refuseSpecCoverageDeactivated (from 42336d9) before DropDisabledRoles + refuseEmptyPhase (from e246b66), so this task is the test that locks that order. Verified by mutation: swapping the two call sites in audit.go makes the new test fail with the empty-phase message on the combined fixture; the swap was reverted and audit.go is byte-identical to its pre-task state.
- A control sub-test ('empty phase alone') runs the identical 'deactivate every auditor' spec shape over a corpus without spec-coverage and gets 'every auditors role is deactivated by this spec: keeper, second', proving the empty-phase condition really is armed by that shape — so in the combined case it is the ordering, not a single condition holding, that selects the message.
- Test 10's precedence clause passes: go test ./... exit 0, golangci-lint run exit 0 (checked as separate exit codes, not a && chain).

tasks.title: Fire refusals only on prompt emission
tasks.acceptance: Neither refusal fires under the review record, status, merge, resolve, resolve-all, verify or report modes. Neither fires under the audit record, status or merge modes. Test 8 asserts the absence of the two literal messages rather than a non-2 exit code.
tasks.closed_reason:
- The two §2.5 refusals are pinned to prompt-emission mode by TestRefusals_FireOnlyOnPromptEmission (internal/cli/domain_lens_test.go): one spec (bothPhasesDeactivatedSpec) deactivates the only reviewer and every auditor including spec-coverage, arming BOTH refusals, and is run through tp review --record/--status/--status --check/--verify and tp audit --record/--status/--status --check, asserting the exits §2.5 item 1 specifies (record and verify 0, status 0, status --check 0 or 1).
- The assertion is the ABSENCE of the two literal messages on stdout and stderr (assertNoRefusalMessage pins "every reviewers/auditors role is deactivated by this spec" and "spec-coverage cannot be deactivated: it carries the entire spec-derived checklist"), never a non-2 exit code, since a malformed argument also exits 2; a control sub-test proves the fixture does refuse under emission for both commands.
- Discriminating power verified by mutation: moving the refusals ahead of the mode branching in newAuditCmd failed both audit --status sub-tests on the absence assertion, and the same mutation in newReviewCmd failed all four review mode sub-tests; both mutations were reverted.
- --merge, --resolve, --resolve-all and --report are not asserted: they take an NDJSON positional and never parse the spec (tp audit registers none of them).
- Out of scope: tp audit writes .tp-review/<spec>/snapshot-audit-round-1.md BEFORE the §2.5 refusal, so a refused audit run still leaves state on disk (observed manually); that is §2.5 item 2, owned by the refusal-before-writes task.

tasks.title: Assert perspective bypasses corpus resolution
tasks.acceptance: The review perspective mode short-circuits before the corpus is resolved. It emits its single fixed prompt carrying neither refusal message. The perspective half of test 8 passes.
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp review --perspective is pinned to carry neither §2.5 refusal: TestRefusals_PerspectiveShortCircuitsBeforeCorpus (internal/cli/domain_lens_test.go) runs all four --perspective values (documentation, testing, code-audit, and regression in its stateless --diff-from/--findings mode (b)) over the shared bothPhasesDeactivatedSpec fixture that arms BOTH refusals, asserting exit 0, non-empty stdout (the prompt was emitted) and assertNoRefusalMessage on stdout+stderr.
- Verified discriminating by mutation: inserting resolveRolePanel(specPath, engine.PhaseReviewers) at the top of runReview (ahead of the perspective dispatch) made all four sub-tests fail with exit 2 and the empty-phase message on stderr; the mutation was reverted and review.go is unchanged by this task.
- A control sub-test re-runs the same fixture through default prompt emission and requires exit 2 plus the empty-phase message, so a silent perspective run measures the short-circuit rather than a toothless fixture.
- Gate green before close: go test ./... exit 0, golangci-lint run exit 0 (checked as separate exit codes, not a && chain).
- The sibling emission-only test's doc comment was updated from 'outside this test's scope' to name the new test, keeping the cross-reference honest.
Out of scope: none observed.

tasks.title: Keep roles_hash free of frontmatter overrides
tasks.acceptance: Toggling enabled changes the recorded round spec_hash. It leaves roles_hash unchanged, proving the override is not fed into ComputeRolesHash. Test 15 passes with the roles_hash clause as the discriminating assertion.

tasks.title: Document the lever in four files
tasks.acceptance: README.md, skills/tp/SKILL.md, skills/tp/REFERENCE.md alongside the role-corpus rule in CLAUDE.md each contain the substring enabled: false deactivates a role for one spec. Each states the disabled-by-spec reason alongside the two emission-only refusals. Each states that domains is the durable axis while a false enabled is the one-spec exception.

tasks.title: State both trim-candidate levers in REFERENCE
tasks.acceptance: REFERENCE.md states that a trim candidate has two levers guarded differently. It states that deleting the role file is unguarded, including for spec-coverage, removing nothing when it is the phase last role file. It states that tp does not guard against deactivating a role with open findings.

tasks.title: Guard the four documents with a test
tasks.acceptance: A guard test asserts the four documents contain the pinned substring. It asserts REFERENCE.md states both trim-candidate levers. Test 17 passes.
